steps.subject: [MC][ELF] Make linked-to symbol name part of ELFSectionKey

evidence: Directly changes MC ELF section identity using the linked-to symbol, a relevant symbol-retention and association mechanism.
Updates AArch64 patchable-function-entry tests and linked-symbol expectations, but does not directly modify emitXRayTable or MCSymbolRefExpr creation.
features: build:make, linked-to-symbol, mc-elf-section-uniquing, patchable-function-entry, path:llvm/include/llvm/MC, path:llvm/lib/MC/MCContext.cpp
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit changes ELF section uniquing so that a section's linked-to symbol name participates in the ELFSectionKey. MCContext::getELFSection now distinguishes otherwise identical ELF sections that have different LinkedToSym values, preventing them from being merged accidentally. The accompanying AArch64 patchable-function-entry tests update expected __patchable_function_entries directives so each section is linked to its own function symbol rather than incorrectly reusing the first function's symbol.
Changed symbols: ELFSectionKey; MCContext::getELFSection; MCContext::renameELFSection; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/patchable-function-entry.ll checks; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/patchable-function-entry-bti.ll checks
Behavioral change: ELF section identity now includes (section name, group name, linked-to symbol name, unique ID), rather than omitting the linked-to symbol name.; Calls to MCContext::getELFSection with the same section/group/unique ID but different LinkedToSym values create or retrieve distinct MCSectionELF instances.; AArch64 patchable-function-entry output is expected to emit __patchable_function_entries sections linked to the corresponding function symbol, including f2, f2_1, f1i, and f3_2, instead of reusing f1.
Assertion or trace link: MCSymbolRefExpr assertion in llvm/lib/MC/MCExpr.cpp; assertion condition: Symbol; llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; AArch64 assembly printer
Reproducer link: The issue involves reduced AArch64 IR with patchable-function-entry metadata.; This commit directly modifies AArch64 patchable-function-entry tests and their __patchable_function_entries section/link-symbol expectations.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM MC ELF section creation and uniquing; AArch64 assembly emission; AsmPrinter/XRay table emission path
Causal explanation: The touched MC logic governs the identity and retained LinkedToSym association of ELF sections. The AArch64 tests demonstrate that patchable-function-entry emission creates repeated __patchable_function_entries sections whose distinguishing property is the linked function symbol. If those sections were incorrectly unified, later emission could observe a section associated with the wrong function symbol, which is materially relevant to symbol-reference construction during the AArch64 AsmPrinter/XRay-table path. However, the retrieved implementation does not directly modify MCSymbolRefExpr::create, emitXRayTable, or AArch64AsmPrinter, so the exact transition from wrong section uniquing to the asserted null/invalid Symbol is not shown.
Causal confidence: 0.78
Build risk: Core MCContext ELF-section uniquing behavior changes, affecting all ELF users that create linked-order sections.; The commit adds dedicated llvm-mc ELF section-combination coverage for the expanded uniquing key.; It updates AArch64 patchable-function-entry and BTI regression expectations, providing directly relevant test coverage.; No retrieved hunk changes the MCSymbolRefExpr assertion site or emitXRayTable itself, limiting direct validation of the reported crash.

diff --git a/llvm/test/MC/ELF/section-combine.s b/llvm/test/MC/ELF/section-combine.s
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..b68eaa3a05af
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/MC/ELF/section-combine.s
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+## Sections are differentiated by the quadruple
+## (section_name, group_name, unique_id, link_to_symbol_name).
+## Sections sharing the same quadruple are combined into one section.
+
+# RUN: llvm-mc -filetype=obj -triple=x86_64 %s -o %t
+# RUN: llvm-readelf -x .foo %t | FileCheck %s
+
+# CHECK:      Hex dump of section '.foo':
+# CHECK-NEXT: 0x00000000 00
+# CHECK:      Hex dump of section '.foo':
+# CHECK-NEXT: 0x00000000 0102
+# CHECK:      Hex dump of section '.foo':
+# CHECK-NEXT: 0x00000000 03
+# CHECK:      Hex dump of section '.foo':
+# CHECK-NEXT: 0x00000000 0405
+# CHECK:      Hex dump of section '.foo':
+# CHECK-NEXT: 0x00000000 06
+# CHECK:      Hex dump of section '.foo':
+# CHECK-NEXT: 0x00000000 0708
+
+foo:
+bar:
+
+## foo and bar are in the same section. However, a section referencing foo
+## is considered different from a section referencing bar.
+.section .foo,"o",@progbits,foo
+.byte 0
+
+.section .foo,"o",@progbits,bar
+.byte 1
+.section .foo,"o",@progbits,bar
+.byte 2
+
+.section .foo,"o",@progbits,bar,unique,0
+.byte 3
+
+.section .foo,"o",@progbits,bar,unique,1
+.byte 4
+.section .foo,"o",@progbits,bar,unique,1
+.byte 5
+
+.section .foo,"Go",@progbits,comdat0,comdat,bar,unique,1
+.byte 6
+
+.section .foo,"Go",@progbits,comdat1,comdat,bar,unique,1
+.byte 7
+.section .foo,"Go",@progbits,comdat1,comdat,bar,unique,1
+.byte 8

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64] Peephole optimization: merge AND and TST instructions
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This AArch64 SelectionDAG peephole change merges an integer AND used by a comparison against zero into an AArch64 ANDS/TST-form node, allowing the logical result and condition flags to be shared. It also updates shift-modulo matching to recognize ANDS as well as generic AND, and adds/updates AArch64 code-generation tests for the resulting instruction selection.
Changed symbols: emitComparison; AArch64DAGToDAGISel::tryShiftAmountMod; isOpcWithIntImmediate; test_func_i32_two_uses; test_func_i64_one_use; fshl_i32; n6_fshl
Behavioral change: In emitComparison, a signed comparison of an AND result with zero now creates an AArch64ISD::ANDS node, replaces all uses of the original ISD::AND result with that node, and returns the ANDS condition-code result.; emitComparison now recognizes an existing AArch64ISD::ANDS operand and directly reuses its condition-code value rather than creating another comparison sequence.; tryShiftAmountMod now accepts an AArch64ISD::ANDS node, in addition to ISD::AND, when recognizing an immediate-masked shift amount.; Generated AArch64 assembly can use ANDS where prior output used AND followed by TST, preserving the AND result when it has non-flag uses.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise ordinary integer AND/compare and funnel-shift lowering; they contain no XRay instrumentation, patchable-function-entry metadata, or symbol-reference emission.; No retrieved hunk modifies MCSymbolRefExpr creation, MCContext symbol ownership, AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, or AArch64AsmPrinter.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SelectionDAG instruction selection and lowering; The reported failure occurs later in AArch64 assembly printing during AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable and MCSymbolRefExpr::create.
Causal explanation: The candidate is directly in the AArch64 code-generation pipeline, so it can change selected machine instructions and condition-code/data dependencies. However, the observed assertion is a null/invalid Symbol contract failure in MCSymbolRefExpr construction from emitXRayTable. The retrieved changes neither handle XRay or patchable-function metadata nor create, lower, retain, or emit MC symbols. The changed AND-to-ANDS optimization therefore has no evidence-backed path to the XRay-table symbol reference that triggers the assertion; target overlap alone is insufficient.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Implementation changes are confined to AArch64 SelectionDAG lowering and DAG instruction selection.; The commit adds a new AArch64 llc/FileCheck regression test and updates existing AArch64 expected assembly, providing targeted coverage of the intended ANDS/TST behavior.; No XRay, AsmPrinter, MC, MCSymbolRefExpr, or patchable-function-entry regression coverage is added.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel subregister-copy selection to avoid creating an intermediate copy in the destination register bank. It adds register-bank minimum-size support, simplifies selectSubregisterCopy to form a COPY directly from the original source register with a subregister operand, and removes selectCopy logic that selected an intermediate destination-bank register class. The accompanying MIR tests update expected COPY sequences and add coverage for truncating an FPR128 value through a subregister copy.
Changed symbols: getMinSizeForRegBank; selectCopy; selectSubregisterCopy; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/GlobalISel/subreg-copy.mir; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/GlobalISel/opt-fold-ext-tbz-tbnz.mir; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/GlobalISel/opt-fold-and-tbz-tbnz.mir
Behavioral change: Adds getMinSizeForRegBank, defining minimum supported sizes of 32 bits for the AArch64 GPR register bank and 8 bits for the FPR bank.; Changes selectSubregisterCopy so the generated subregister COPY reads SrcReg directly, rather than first building an intermediate full-register COPY.; Removes selectCopy's construction of a destination-bank register class sized like the source and the associated call that inserted the prior two-step subregister-copy sequence.; Reduces generated GlobalISel COPY chains for cross-bank subregister copies, as reflected by updated MIR expectations.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The added and modified tests exercise AArch64 GlobalISel instruction selection and subregister COPY formation, not XRay patchable-function-entry metadata or XRay table emission.; No retrieved hunk mentions MCSymbolRefExpr, MCSymbol, emitXRayTable, XRay, or patchable-function-entry.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 GlobalISel instruction selection; The reported failure occurs later in AArch64 assembly printing through llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable and llvm::MCSymbolRefExpr::create.
Causal explanation: The change is in the same target backend and can alter MachineInstr sequences eventually consumed by assembly emission, so it has a broad upstream reachability relationship to an AArch64 llc failure. However, the retrieved change is narrowly about register-bank/subregister COPY selection and contains no symbol creation, MC-expression handling, AsmPrinter logic, XRay table emission, or patchable-function metadata lowering. The reported assertion requires an invalid/null symbol at MCSymbolRefExpr creation during emitXRayTable, for which these hunks provide no concrete causal path. Therefore the evidence supports only a weak, indirect link.
Causal confidence: 0.07
Build risk: The implementation change is confined to AArch64InstructionSelector.cpp and is accompanied by AArch64 GlobalISel MIR regression coverage.; New MIR coverage runs llc with -run-pass=instruction-select and -verify-machineinstrs, which checks the altered instruction-selection behavior.; No retrieved end-to-end AArch64 assembly-emission, XRay, emitXRayTable, or MCSymbolRefExpr regression test validates the reported crash path.

Summary: Adds AArch64 SVE contiguous prefetch intrinsic support. The change introduces the llvm.aarch64.sve.prf intrinsic, SelectionDAG address-selection support for its non-MemSDNode intrinsic form, SVE prefetch instruction-selection patterns for predicate widths, and llc coverage verifying generated prfb/prfh/prfw/prfd encodings and addressing forms.
Changed symbols: getPackedVectorTypeFromPredicateType; getMemVTFromNode; AArch64DAGToDAGISel::SelectAddrModeIndexedSVE; sve_prefetch; int_aarch64_sve_prf; am_sve_indexed_s6
Behavioral change: AArch64 SelectionDAG address matching no longer requires every root to be a MemSDNode; it can derive a memory vector type for ISD::INTRINSIC_VOID nodes representing Intrinsic::aarch64_sve_prf.; For SVE prefetches, the memory element/vector width is inferred from the scalable i1 predicate width, producing a packed scalable integer vector totaling one SVE block.; Adds instruction-selection patterns that lower llvm.aarch64.sve.prf for nxv16i1, nxv8i1, nxv4i1, and nxv2i1 predicates to contiguous SVE prefetch instructions with immediate, register-indexed, and zero-offset address forms.; The previous assertion in SelectAddrModeIndexedSVE is replaced by a failure return when no memory type can be derived.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The added tests invoke llc for an AArch64 triple, but exercise SVE prefetch intrinsics rather than XRay or patchable-function-entry metadata.; No retrieved hunk adds or changes MCSymbolRefExpr construction, MC symbol ownership, emitXRayTable, or XRay table data.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SelectionDAG instruction selection; AArch64 SVE instruction definitions; LLVM IR intrinsic definitions
Causal explanation: The candidate is in the AArch64 code-generation pipeline, which is consistent with the target component named by the crash. However, its substantive behavior is restricted to lowering and address selection for a new SVE prefetch intrinsic before assembly printing. The reported failure occurs in MCSymbolRefExpr::create from AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable and is associated with XRay patchable-function-entry metadata; none of those paths or symbols is changed here. The retrieved evidence therefore provides only broad target-pipeline proximity, not an evidence-backed mechanism connecting this SVE prefetch change to the invalid/null symbol assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Adds a new AArch64 intrinsic declaration and TableGen instruction-selection patterns, so generated intrinsic and instruction-definition artifacts must remain synchronized.; Adds llc/FileCheck coverage using -mtriple=aarch64-linux-gnu -mattr=+sve for contiguous prefetch encodings and address-offset boundaries.; The modified selector deliberately replaces a hard assertion with a false return for roots lacking a recoverable memory type, reducing assertion risk in that selector but not covering the reported MC/XRay assertion.

For SVE prefetches, the memory element/vector width is inferred from the scalable i1 predicate width, producing a packed scalable integer vector totaling one SVE block.

Adds instruction-selection patterns that lower llvm.aarch64.sve.prf for nxv16i1, nxv8i1, nxv4i1, and nxv2i1 predicates to contiguous SVE prefetch instructions with immediate, register-indexed, and zero-offset address forms.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64 Windows EH frame layout so the UnwindHelp slot is created as a fixed stack object rather than as a normal stack object. It centralizes computation of the Win64 fixed-object area, including varargs storage and an 8-byte UnwindHelp object when EH funclets exist, and makes frame-index reference selection fall back to the normal frame-reference logic unless SP updates are explicitly ignored.
Changed symbols: AArch64FrameLowering::processFunctionBeforeFrameFinalized; AArch64FrameLowering::emitPrologue; AArch64FrameLowering::emitEpilogue; AArch64FrameLowering::getFrameIndexReferencePreferSP; getFixedObjectSize; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/wineh-unwindhelp-via-fp.ll
Behavioral change: Replaces creation of the 8-byte Win64 EH UnwindHelp slot with CreateFixedObject using an SP offset derived from the complete fixed-object area.; Introduces getFixedObjectSize, which accounts for aligned Win64 varargs storage plus an UnwindHelp object when the primary function has EH funclets; it returns zero for non-Win64 functions and funclets.; Uses the centralized fixed-object-size calculation in prologue, epilogue, and frame-pointer-offset computations so stack layout remains consistent.; Changes getFrameIndexReferencePreferSP to use an SP-relative object offset only when IgnoreSPUpdates is set; otherwise it delegates to getFrameIndexReference, allowing frame-pointer-based addressing where required.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64 assembly printer
Reproducer link: The added test exercises AArch64 Windows EH funclets and fixed UnwindHelp placement, not XRay patchable-function-entry metadata.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 frame lowering; AArch64 Windows EH stack-frame layout
Causal explanation: The commit is in the AArch64 backend and therefore runs before assembly emission, matching the target portion of the failing llc pipeline. However, the retrieved changes do not touch AArch64AsmPrinter, AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, XRay instrumentation or metadata lowering, MCExpr, MCSymbolRefExpr creation, or symbol/reference handling. Its explicit scope is Windows EH fixed-stack-object addressing, whereas the reported crash occurs while emitting an XRay table and asserting that an MCSymbolRefExpr has a Symbol. The available hunks provide no evidence that this frame-layout change can create the null/invalid symbol condition required by that assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Implementation-only change is confined to llvm/lib/Target/AArch64/AArch64FrameLowering.cpp.; Adds an llc/FileCheck regression test for aarch64-windows EH funclet stack addressing.; The change modifies shared prologue, epilogue, and frame-index reference calculations for Win64 AArch64 functions, so Windows EH code-generation regressions are plausible.; No retrieved test covers XRay, patchable-function-entry metadata, emitXRayTable, or MCSymbolRefExpr behavior.

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64][Fix] LdSt optimization generate premature stack-popping
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit restricts the AArch64 load/store optimizer's formation of post-indexed stack-pointer updates. In AArch64LoadStoreOpt::findMatchingUpdateInsnForward, it now rejects SP post-increment optimization when an intervening instruction may access memory, and disables the optimization for Windows CFI functions requiring unwind entries. It adds a MIR regression test for avoiding a premature SP pop.
Changed symbols: AArch64LoadStoreOpt::findMatchingUpdateInsnForward; AArch64LoadStoreOptimizer.cpp; llvm::MCAsmInfo; aarch64-ldst-no-premature-sp-pop.mir
Behavioral change: Treats an intervening load or store as a barrier when considering a stack-pointer-based load/store plus update optimization.; Prevents SP post-increment formation across potentially memory-accessing instructions, avoiding an update that would pop the stack before intervening accesses.; Avoids this SP optimization for Windows CFI functions that need unwind-table entries, preserving unwind/debug-information consistency.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The added MIR test exercises AArch64 stack-pointer load/store optimization and checks that a post-indexed stack store is not produced before the final stack adjustment.; No retrieved hunk contains XRay instrumentation, patchable-function-entry metadata, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr construction, or MC symbol-reference handling.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64LoadStoreOpt machine-function optimization; AArch64 code generation
Causal explanation: The commit is in the AArch64 backend, which overlaps the target named in the crash trace, but its substantive change is confined to pre-assembly machine-instruction optimization of SP-relative load/store updates. The reported failure occurs later in AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable while creating an MCSymbolRefExpr and is tied to XRay patchable-function-entry metadata. The retrieved changes neither create nor modify symbols, XRay tables, assembly emission, or MC expressions. Moreover, the change adds conservative rejection conditions rather than introducing new post-indexed SP transformations. Therefore the available evidence does not support this commit as a cause of the assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.04

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64][GlobalISel] Avoid copies to target register bank for subregister copies
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel handling of cross-bank subregister copies. It removes an intermediate copy into a destination-bank register class and instead constructs the subregister COPY directly from the original source register. It also adds register-bank minimum-size classification and updates/adds MIR instruction-selection tests to expect the shorter copy sequences.
Changed symbols: getMinSizeForRegBank; selectCopy; selectSubregisterCopy
Behavioral change: selectSubregisterCopy no longer materializes an intermediate full-register COPY before creating the subregister COPY; the resulting COPY uses SrcReg directly with the selected subregister.; selectCopy no longer obtains a destination-bank register class sized like the source and no longer invokes selectSubregisterCopy through the removed cross-bank-copy path shown in the hunk.; The new getMinSizeForRegBank helper defines minimum AArch64 GPR and FPR bank sizes as 32 and 8 bits, respectively.; GlobalISel MIR expectations change from a full-width copy followed by a subregister copy to a direct subregister copy, reducing generated copy instructions.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The added and modified tests exercise llc AArch64 GlobalISel instruction selection with subregister copies.; No retrieved test uses XRay, patchable-function-entry metadata, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr, or MC symbol construction.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 GlobalISel instruction selection; MachineInstr COPY and subregister-copy selection
Causal explanation: The candidate is in the AArch64 backend, so it can affect machine-code generation before assembly printing. However, the retrieved changes are confined to GlobalISel register-bank/subregister COPY selection. They do not modify AArch64AsmPrinter, AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, MCExpr/MCSymbolRefExpr creation, XRay lowering, or patchable-function-entry metadata handling. The reported failure occurs when emitXRayTable creates an MCSymbolRefExpr and asserts that its Symbol is valid; the shown copy-selection changes provide no evidence of changing the XRay table symbol or its lifetime. Thus the AArch64 overlap is only indirect and does not establish a causal mechanism for this assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Adds a focused MIR regression test executed with llc -run-pass=instruction-select -verify-machineinstrs.; Updates existing AArch64 GlobalISel MIR FileCheck expectations for reduced COPY sequences.; The shown test coverage validates instruction selection only, not full assembly emission, XRay table emission, or MC symbol-reference creation.

behavioral_change: Introduces an AArch64 IR-level ModulePass that recognizes SVE convert.to.svbool and convert.from.svbool intrinsics and removes eligible redundant reinterpret sequences.
The pass also declares optimization paths for SVE ptest intrinsic and PHI-node patterns, with DominatorTreeWrapperPass required and CFG preservation declared.
Adds the pass to AArch64 code generation only at aggressive optimization level when EnableSVEIntrinsicOpts is true.
Adds focused AArch64 tests for ptest and svbool reinterpret optimization behavior, including cases intentionally left untransformed when operand shapes or lane semantics differ.

reproducer: The retrieved change contains no XRay, emitXRayTable, patchable-function-entry, MCSymbolRefExpr, MCSymbol, or MCExpr use.
The visible tests exercise SVE intrinsic IR transformations rather than XRay metadata emission or AArch64 assembly-printer symbol references.
issue_link.explanation: The commit is in the AArch64 compilation pipeline and could indirectly alter IR reaching later code generation, but the changed pass is narrowly about SVE svbool conversions, ptest operations, and PHIs. The crash occurs later in AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable while creating an MCSymbolRefExpr, and no retrieved hunk changes AArch64 assembly emission, XRay table generation, MC symbol/reference handling, or patchable-function-entry lowering. The issue context also does not establish that the reproducer contains SVE IR or runs at the aggressive optimization level required to enable this pass. Thus the available evidence supports only a weak, indirect causal link.

build_risk: Adds a new AArch64CodeGen compilation unit, SVEIntrinsicOpts.cpp, and declares its factory in AArch64.h.
Wires a new legacy ModulePass into the AArch64 O3/aggressive pipeline and adds a pipeline-order test.
Adds dedicated CodeGen/AArch64 tests for the new pass, but no regression test covers XRay table emission, patchable-function-entry metadata, or MCSymbolRefExpr assertions.

Summary: This NFC-labelled MC-section naming refactor moves section-name storage/use toward the base MCSection interface and updates section construction and diagnostics accordingly. In the visible hunks, MCContext::getMachOSection changes its uniquing-map insertion flow, derives the Mach-O section name from the map-owned combined key, and adds validation that Mach-O section names are at most 16 bytes and contain no NUL. Derived ELF, Wasm, and XCOFF section constructors pass their names to MCSection, while MCAssembler diagnostics use the generic MCSection::getName().
Changed symbols: llvm::MCContext::getMachOSection; llvm::MCSection::MCSection; llvm::MCSectionMachO; llvm::MCSectionELF; llvm::MCSectionWasm; llvm::MCSectionXCOFF; llvm::MCAssembler::writeSectionData

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit makes AArch64 SVE floating-point conversion intrinsics use predicates whose scalable vector lane counts match the relevant conversion/result types, rather than the prior fixed nxv16i1 predicate convention. It updates Clang builtin lowering, AArch64 intrinsic declarations, TableGen instruction-selection patterns, and ACLE builtin type descriptions accordingly.
Changed symbols: CodeGenFunction::EmitAArch64SVEBuiltinExpr; Builtin_SVCVT; int_aarch64_sve_fcvtzs_*; int_aarch64_sve_fcvtzu_*; int_aarch64_sve_fcvt_*; int_aarch64_sve_scvtf_*; int_aarch64_sve_ucvtf_*; sve2_fp_convert_down_narrow
Behavioral change: Clang no longer special-cases FP-conversion predicates as <vscale x 16 x i1> when emitting AArch64 SVE builtins; it casts predicates to the normal SVE type selected by TypeFlags.; The Builtin_SVCVT intrinsic template now accepts an explicit predicate type, and individual conversion intrinsics select narrower predicate vectors such as nxv4i1 or nxv2i1 where appropriate.; AArch64 SVE instruction-selection patterns are changed to require predicate lane counts matching the conversion pattern instead of nxv16i1.; ACLE builtin descriptions are adjusted for the revised intrinsic typing and overload behavior.

Reproducer link: The reported reproducer involves XRay patchable-function-entry metadata and reaches AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable.; The retrieved changes concern SVE FP-conversion intrinsic typing and contain no XRay, patchable-function-entry, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr, MCContext, or symbol-reference emission changes.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SVE frontend builtin lowering; AArch64 SelectionDAG/TableGen instruction selection; Clang ACLE SVE builtin definitions

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds AArch64 SVE lowering for scalable-vector signed and unsigned division. The change introduces target-specific predicated SDIV/UDIV DAG nodes, marks scalable-vector ISD::SDIV and ISD::UDIV operations as custom-lowered, converts matching SVE intrinsics into those nodes, and maps them to the existing SVE division instruction definitions. A new AArch64 llc test verifies emission of predicated SVE sdiv and udiv instructions.
Changed symbols: AArch64TargetLowering::LowerDIV; AArch64TargetLowering::LowerOperation; AArch64TargetLowering::AArch64TargetLowering; performIntrinsicCombine; AArch64ISD::SDIV_PRED; AArch64ISD::UDIV_PRED; AArch64sdiv_pred; AArch64udiv_pred
Behavioral change: Scalable-vector ISD::SDIV and ISD::UDIV operations are custom-lowered through LowerDIV rather than their prior lowering path.; LowerDIV requires both operands to be scalable vectors, constructs an all-true SVE predicate, and creates an AArch64 predicated division DAG node.; AArch64 SVE signed/unsigned division intrinsics are combined directly into SDIV_PRED and UDIV_PRED nodes.; The SVE SDIV_ZPmZ and UDIV_ZPmZ instruction patterns now match the new AArch64-specific division DAG nodes.; The new test expects llc with aarch64-linux-gnu and +sve to emit ptrue followed by predicated sdiv or udiv instructions.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The retrieved test exercises AArch64 scalable-vector SVE division, not XRay patchable-function-entry metadata or XRay table generation.; No retrieved hunk creates or passes an MCSymbolRefExpr, changes MC symbol/reference handling, or mentions emitXRayTable.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 SelectionDAG lowering; AArch64 SVE instruction selection; AArch64 code generation
Causal explanation: The commit is in the AArch64 backend and can affect machine code that later reaches the assembly printer, so it has a broad target-level connection to the failing compilation pipeline. However, the retrieved changes are limited to SVE vector division lowering and instruction patterns. They do not modify AArch64AsmPrinter, AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, XRay instrumentation or metadata lowering, MCExpr/MCSymbolRefExpr construction, or symbol lifetime/ownership. The issue's specific failure is an MCSymbolRefExpr Symbol assertion during XRay table emission, for which these hunks provide no concrete causal mechanism.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Adds a focused AArch64 CodeGen regression test runnable with llc -mtriple=aarch64-linux-gnu -mattr=+sve.; The test validates textual SVE instruction emission only; it does not cover XRay instrumentation, patchable-function-entry metadata, XRay table emission, or MC symbol-reference assertions.; Changes TableGen DAG-pattern bindings and SelectionDAG custom lowering, which can affect AArch64 SVE code-generation coverage but has no retrieved build-system change.

steps.subject: [XRay] Change ARM/AArch64/powerpc64le to use version 2 sled (PC-relative address)

evidence: Directly modifies AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, which appears in the crash stack immediately before MCSymbolRefExpr creation.
Changes AArch64 XRay sleds to version 2 and changes table entries to PC-relative symbol-difference expressions using new temporary labels.
features: aarch64-asmprinter, emit-xray-table, mc-symbol-reference, meta:core-llvm, path:compiler-rt/lib/xray/xray_AArch64.cpp, path:compiler-rt/lib/xray/xray_arm.cpp
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes XRay sled/table emission for ARM, AArch64, and PowerPC to use XRay sled version 2 and changes generic AsmPrinter XRay-table addressing to PC-relative on every target except MIPS. On AArch64, EmitSled now records version 2 sleds, while AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable emits PC-relative table entries; the accompanying AArch64 test changes expected .xword entries from absolute sled-label references to differences between sled labels and newly emitted temporary labels.
Changed symbols: llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; llvm::AArch64AsmPrinter::EmitSled; llvm::ARMAsmPrinter::EmitSled; llvm::PPCLinuxAsmPrinter::emitInstruction; xray_AArch64::patchSled; recordSled
Behavioral change: AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable changes the PC-relative-address predicate from x86-only to every non-MIPS target.; AArch64 XRay sleds are recorded as version 2 through recordSled(CurSled, MI, Kind, 2).; AArch64 XRay-table assembly changes from absolute .xword sled-symbol entries to PC-relative symbol-difference expressions such as .Lxray_sled_0-.Ltmp2.; The AArch64 XRay runtime reads a sled address through Sled.address() rather than directly through Sled.Address, consistent with the version-2 representation.
Assertion or trace link: llvm::MCSymbolRefExpr::create; assertion: Symbol; llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; AArch64 Assembly Printer; llvm/lib/MC/MCExpr.cpp
Reproducer link: The issue is an llc crash on reduced AArch64 IR involving XRay patchable-function-entry metadata.; This commit directly changes the AArch64 XRay sled format and the generic XRay-table address-expression form reached while emitting those sled records.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 Assembly Printer; AsmPrinter XRay table emission; MC symbol/reference expressions; XRay sled lowering and runtime format
Causal explanation: The crash trace directly reaches AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable and fails in MCSymbolRefExpr::create on its required Symbol invariant. This commit modifies that exact XRay-table emission path to use PC-relative label-difference expressions on AArch64, and simultaneously changes AArch64 sled records to version 2. The updated AArch64 test confirms that this path now creates and uses temporary labels alongside sled symbols. These changes plausibly expose an invalid, missing, or otherwise unsuitable symbol while constructing the new MC expression. The retrieved hunks do not show the exact failing MCSymbolRefExpr::create call or prove which symbol is null, so the causal mechanism cannot be established beyond the direct path and format change.
Causal confidence: 0.86
Build risk: Changes shared AsmPrinter XRay-table behavior for all non-MIPS targets, increasing cross-target regression surface.; Changes the on-disk/assembly representation expected by XRay sled version 2 and requires consistency between compiler emission and compiler-rt runtime decoding.; An AArch64 CodeGen test was updated to validate the new PC-relative table layout, but no retrieved test specifically exercises the crashing patchable-function-entry metadata reproducer or an MCSymbolRefExpr assertion case.

steps.subject: [AArch64][GlobalISel] Fix sub-64b stack parameter passing on Darwin.

evidence: AArch64 GlobalISel call-lowering change can affect generated machine code before emission.
The changed mechanism is stack argument extension/layout, not XRay function symbols or MC expression construction.
features: aarch64, call-lowering, globalisel, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/include/llvm/CodeGen, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/GlobalISel
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel outgoing-call argument lowering for stack-passed arguments. It removes special handling that widened arguments with AExt location information to the location VT before storing them, and adds GlobalISel calling-convention tests covering sub-64-bit i8/i16 stack arguments on Darwin and non-Darwin targets.
Changed symbols: OutgoingArgHandler; AArch64CallLowering; i8i16caller test checks; caller_s128 test checks
Behavioral change: OutgoingArgHandler no longer applies G_ANYEXT to an outgoing argument solely because its CCValAssign location info is AExt before writing it to a stack argument slot.; Sub-64-bit outgoing stack arguments are therefore stored at their assigned argument size/layout rather than being widened to the location VT size.; The added tests expect compact Darwin stack layout for i8/i16 arguments (6-byte call frame with stores at offsets 0, 2, 4, and 5), while the non-Darwin test retains 8-byte slot spacing and a 32-byte call frame.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; llc; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise AArch64 GlobalISel call lowering for integer stack arguments and varargs-style calling-convention cases.; No retrieved hunk mentions XRay, patchable-function-entry metadata, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr, MCContext, or symbol-reference construction.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 GlobalISel call lowering; IRTranslator-stage CodeGen tests
Causal explanation: The candidate is in the AArch64 backend and can affect MachineInstr/stack-argument formation before later assembly emission, so it is broadly upstream of the reported AArch64 compilation path. However, the observed failure is an MCSymbolRefExpr Symbol assertion reached through AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, whereas this change only adjusts GlobalISel outgoing stack-argument extension behavior. The accompanying tests stop after irtranslator and do not exercise assembly printing or XRay table emission. The retrieved evidence therefore provides no concrete causal path from this change to creation of a null/invalid MC symbol reference for XRay metadata.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Implementation change is limited to llvm/lib/Target/AArch64/AArch64CallLowering.cpp.; Regression coverage was added in AArch64 GlobalISel calling-convention tests for both Darwin and non-Darwin layouts.; Test RUN lines were updated to remove stderr redirection and annotate autogenerated checks.; No retrieved crash-regression test reaches the AsmPrinter, MC layer, or XRay emission path.

causal_evidence.summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel outgoing-call argument lowering for stack-passed arguments. It removes special handling that widened arguments with AExt location information to the location VT before storing them, and adds GlobalISel calling-convention tests covering sub-64-bit i8/i16 stack arguments on Darwin and non-Darwin targets.
behavioral_change: OutgoingArgHandler no longer applies G_ANYEXT to an outgoing argument solely because its CCValAssign location info is AExt before writing it to a stack argument slot.
Sub-64-bit outgoing stack arguments are therefore stored at their assigned argument size/layout rather than being widened to the location VT size.

The added tests expect compact Darwin stack layout for i8/i16 arguments (6-byte call frame with stores at offsets 0, 2, 4, and 5), while the non-Darwin test retains 8-byte slot spacing and a 32-byte call frame.

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64][GlobalISel] Fix sub-64b stack parameter passing on Darwin.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes AArch64 GlobalISel outgoing-call argument lowering for stack-passed arguments. It removes special handling that widened arguments with AExt location information to the location VT before storing them, and adds GlobalISel calling-convention tests covering sub-64-bit i8/i16 stack arguments on Darwin and non-Darwin targets.
Changed symbols: OutgoingArgHandler; AArch64CallLowering; i8i16caller test checks; caller_s128 test checks
Behavioral change: OutgoingArgHandler no longer applies G_ANYEXT to an outgoing argument solely because its CCValAssign location info is AExt before writing it to a stack argument slot.; Sub-64-bit outgoing stack arguments are therefore stored at their assigned argument size/layout rather than being widened to the location VT size.; The added tests expect compact Darwin stack layout for i8/i16 arguments (6-byte call frame with stores at offsets 0, 2, 4, and 5), while the non-Darwin test retains 8-byte slot spacing and a 32-byte call frame.
Assertion or trace link: AArch64; llc; assembly printer
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise AArch64 GlobalISel call lowering for integer stack arguments and varargs-style calling-convention cases.; No retrieved hunk mentions XRay, patchable-function-entry metadata, emitXRayTable, MCSymbolRefExpr, MCContext, or symbol-reference construction.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 GlobalISel call lowering; IRTranslator-stage CodeGen tests
Causal explanation: The candidate is in the AArch64 backend and can affect MachineInstr/stack-argument formation before later assembly emission, so it is broadly upstream of the reported AArch64 compilation path. However, the observed failure is an MCSymbolRefExpr Symbol assertion reached through AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable, whereas this change only adjusts GlobalISel outgoing stack-argument extension behavior. The accompanying tests stop after irtranslator and do not exercise assembly printing or XRay table emission. The retrieved evidence therefore provides no concrete causal path from this change to creation of a null/invalid MC symbol reference for XRay metadata.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Implementation change is limited to llvm/lib/Target/AArch64/AArch64CallLowering.cpp.; Regression coverage was added in AArch64 GlobalISel calling-convention tests for both Darwin and non-Darwin layouts.; Test RUN lines were updated to remove stderr redirection and annotate autogenerated checks.; No retrieved crash-regression test reaches the AsmPrinter, MC layer, or XRay emission path.

behavioral_change: OutgoingArgHandler no longer applies G_ANYEXT to an outgoing argument solely because its CCValAssign location info is AExt before writing it to a stack argument slot.

The added tests expect compact Darwin stack layout for i8/i16 arguments (6-byte call frame with stores at offsets 0, 2, 4, and 5), while the non-Darwin test retains 8-byte slot spacing and a 32-byte call frame.

Summary: This commit substantially rewrites XRay sled-table emission in AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable for sled version 2: rather than constructing a Location expression and delegating the location/function fields to XRayFunctionEntry::emit, it emits two explicit word-sized MC expressions for PC-relative sled and function-begin addresses, while retaining symbol-value emission in the alternate branch. It also narrows XRayFunctionEntry::emit to the remaining entry payload and expands SetupMachineFunction handling for functions carrying function-instrument or xray-instruction-threshold attributes.
Changed symbols: llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; llvm::AsmPrinter::XRayFunctionEntry::emit; llvm::AsmPrinter::SetupMachineFunction
Behavioral change: XRay sled version-2 table emission now directly constructs and emits MCBinaryExpr/MCSymbolRefExpr expressions for Sled.Sled relative to a temporary Dot symbol and for CurrentFnBegin relative to Dot plus one word.; The table emitter adds a new MCSymbolRefExpr::create(CurrentFnBegin, Ctx) call; prior code only built the shown Location expression from Sled.Sled and Dot, then separately passed CurrentFnSym to XRayFunctionEntry::emit.; Responsibility for emitting the sled location and current-function symbol/value fields moves out of XRayFunctionEntry::emit and into emitXRayTable; the entry emitter signature drops its Location and CurrentFnSym parameters.; SetupMachineFunction's shown condition is extended to recognize function-instrument and xray-instruction-threshold function attributes.
Assertion or trace link: llvm::MCSymbolRefExpr::create; MCSymbolRefExpr assertion; Symbol assertion failure; llvm::AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable; AArch64 Assembly Printer
Reproducer link: The reported reduced AArch64 input reaches XRay patchable-function-entry table generation during llc assembly printing.; The retrieved hunk changes the exact XRay table-emission function named in the crash stack and adds symbol-reference construction there.; No retrieved test or execution result directly demonstrates the reduced reproducer failing after this commit.
Pass or subsystem link: CodeGen AsmPrinter; XRay sled/table emission; MC expression and symbol-reference construction; AArch64 assembly-printer execution path
Causal explanation: The crash is directly reachable from AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable and fails in MCSymbolRefExpr construction with the Symbol assertion. This commit modifies that exact function and introduces a new MCSymbolRefExpr based on CurrentFnBegin as part of the version-2 PC-relative function-address record. Thus, if CurrentFnBegin is absent or otherwise invalid for the affected XRay/patchable-function case, this newly introduced reference is a direct plausible assertion trigger. The hunks do not themselves establish that CurrentFnBegin is null for the reproducer, so the exact bad symbol value remains unproven, but the stack/function/API overlap is unusually specific.
Causal confidence: 0.95
Build risk: The XRayFunctionEntry::emit declaration and definition both change signature, requiring all callers to be updated; the shown emitXRayTable call is updated.; No retrieved test hunk covers AArch64, XRay, sled version 2, or patchable-function-entry behavior.; The commit does not modify llvm/lib/MC/MCExpr.cpp or the MCSymbolRefExpr assertion contract; its risk is through a new caller-side symbol reference.; No retrieved hunk changes an AArch64-specific source file, but AsmPrinter::emitXRayTable is on the reported AArch64 assembly-printer stack and is shared by target printers.
